log.detail: T10-F-001: the contact-import re-walk is itself bounded at 16 pages and its flag is consumed regardless, so a message behind >16 pages of poison is permanently lost

Verifier returned DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, but the orchestrator declines to accept: T10R3-F-001 (major) is silent permanent message loss when a recovery poll is interrupted with Ctrl-C, which is a normal way to stop a poll and is not an acceptable residual before deployment. Confirmed by reading the source, not only from the report: takeMailboxRewalk() deletes the position before the walk and it is written back only on return, so the whole walk is a crash window. Also carrying T10R3-F-002 (ack-route count oracle) and T10R3-F-003 (RelayClient loopback hostname rule) into the fix.

tasks.dispositionReason: 17 tests: 8 RED (4 loopback, 3 re-walk crash safety, 1 ack-oracle) and 9 green guards including the T6-F-004 guard RED-4b. Re-verified by the orchestrator's own runs: pnpm test 293 tests / 7 failed, all in the two new vitest files; go test ./... exactly one failure, the ack oracle, every other package ok. RED-4's cursorless line re-stated under ruling; the ack range test given a V2-signing legitimate-client helper with every assertion byte-identical.

tasks.title: Fix T10R3-F-001 re-walk crash safety, T10R3-F-002 ack oracle, T10R3-F-003 loopback rule
tasks.dispositionReason: All eight handover REDs green; re-verified by the orchestrator's own runs on this tree: pnpm test exit 0 (36 files / 228 tests in apps/cli, every package green, 293 total), test:e2e 3/3 exit 0, typecheck exit 0, go test -race -count=1 -tags relayv2 ./... exit 0 with 8 packages ok and 0 data races. All five test-file SHA-256 digests match T15's recorded values exactly, so the specification was not edited to fit the fix. The T6-F-004 trap was not taken: the position is still cleared, on the same condition, and both guards hold.
